rows.source: HSE woodworking-machinery safety guidance
rows.verified: HSE's woodworking-machinery Approved Code of Practice applies to most fixed woodworking machinery but generally excludes hand-held tools.

rows.source: HSE woodworking-machinery safety guidance
rows.verified: The guidance covers machinery used on wood, corkboard, fibreboard and composite materials.

rows.source: HSE woodworking-machinery safety guidance
rows.verified: Employers, managers and supervisors responsible for woodworking machinery must ensure it is used safely.

rows.source: HSE woodworking-machinery safety guidance
rows.verified: Operators need suitable information, instruction and practical training before using machinery.

rows.source: HSE woodworking-machinery safety guidance
rows.verified: Machine guarding and protection devices must be selected and used for the particular machine and operation.

rows.source: HSE woodworking-machinery safety guidance
rows.verified: General training should include dust extraction, lifting aids, suitable personal protection, housekeeping and awareness of other operators.

rows.source: HSE woodworking-machinery safety guidance
rows.verified: Machine-specific training should cover hazards such as kickback, dropping-on, taking-off, machine limitations and common accident causes.

rows.source: HSE woodworking-machinery safety guidance
rows.verified: Safe operation includes correct use of guards, jigs, push-sticks, brakes, dust extraction and suitable tooling.

rows.source: HSE woodworking-machinery safety guidance
rows.verified: Woodworking-machinery risk depends on machine type, guarding, cutters and tooling, feed method, kickback, braking, extraction, maintenance, materials and operator competence.

rows.source: HSE woodworking-machinery safety guidance
rows.verified: General guarding, braking, tooling, extraction, training and safe operation of woodworking machinery guidance does not prove current conditions or control performance at an individual parcel and does not establish an exact incident, exposure or illness probability.

rows.source: HSE ionising-radiation protection and notification guidance
rows.verified: Ionising radiation includes X-rays, gamma rays, radioactive sources and naturally occurring radiation such as radon.

rows.source: HSE ionising-radiation protection and notification guidance
rows.verified: People can be exposed externally or internally through inhalation, ingestion or contamination of wounds.

rows.source: HSE ionising-radiation protection and notification guidance
rows.verified: Employers must protect workers and the public and keep ionising-radiation exposure as low as reasonably practicable and below dose limits.

rows.source: HSE ionising-radiation protection and notification guidance
rows.verified: A radiation risk assessment must be completed before a new ionising-radiation activity begins and reviewed after significant change.

rows.source: HSE ionising-radiation protection and notification guidance
rows.verified: Engineering controls and design features should be used before safe systems of work and personal protective equipment.

rows.source: HSE ionising-radiation protection and notification guidance
rows.verified: Most work must be notified to HSE or covered by registration or consent according to whether it is low, medium or high risk.

rows.source: HSE ionising-radiation protection and notification guidance
rows.verified: Risk assessment should estimate potential doses, determine the need for personal dose monitoring and identify employees who may need classification.

rows.source: HSE ionising-radiation protection and notification guidance
rows.verified: Dose records, local rules, emergency arrangements and cooperation between employers are required where relevant to the work and controlled areas.

rows.source: HSE ionising-radiation protection and notification guidance
rows.verified: Ionising-radiation risk depends on source type and activity, energy, shielding, distance, time, contamination routes, work practice, accident potential and dose monitoring.

rows.source: HSE ionising-radiation protection and notification guidance
rows.verified: General risk assessment, exposure restriction, notification, registration, consent and dose monitoring guidance does not prove current conditions or control performance at an individual parcel and does not establish an exact incident, exposure or illness probability.
